memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Be very strong; be careful to obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, without turning aside to the right or to the left. Do not associate with these nations that remain among you; do not invoke the names of their gods or swear by them. You must not serve them or bow down to them. But you are to hold fast to the Lord your God, as you have until now." — Josh 23:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Be very strong." It takes strength not only to fight battles but to stay faithful. Joshua urges the people to hold to God's word without turning aside to the right or the left — no drifting, no compromise. And then he names the real danger: the surrounding nations and their gods.

The warning was not against the people themselves but against their idols. Israel was to have nothing to do with those gods — not to name them, swear by them, serve them or bow to them. Instead, they were to "hold fast to the Lord."

That phrase, "hold fast," is tender and strong at once. It pictures clinging to God the way you would cling to someone you love and refuse to let go. This is the heart of faithfulness — not cold rule-keeping, but a devoted grip on the God who has been good to us.

The pull of the world is real for us too. The idols may look different today — money, status, comfort, approval — but the call is the same: do not bow to them; hold fast to the Lord. Jesus said no one can serve two masters (Matt 6:24). Our hearts were made to cling to God alone. Take courage, be strong, and keep your grip firmly on Him, "as you have until now."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "gods" of today most tempt you to turn aside from the Lord?
2. What does it look like for you to "hold fast" to God this week?
3. Where do you need strength to stay faithful without compromise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me strength to hold fast to You without turning aside. Keep my heart from the idols around me, for I want to cling to You alone. Amen.
